en: The Sūtra on the Merit of Counting Beads from the Mañjuśrī Dhāraṇī-piṭaka,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śramaṇa Śikṣānanda of the Great Tang Dynasty.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī Dharmaputra rose from his seat amidst the great assembly, adjusted his robes, bared his right shoulder, joined his palms in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Now, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, I wish to speak of the merit of receiving and maintaining the rosary, and to calculate the distinctions in the benefits of its share of blessings.
I only pray that the World-Honored One will compassionately grant me permission to do so.
The Buddha said to Mañjuśrī:
“Excellent, excellent!
Listen as you explain it.”
The Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī said:

"If there are good men or good women who are able to recite and maintain various dhāraṇīs and the names of the Buddhas—desiring to benefit themselves and protect others, and wishing to swiftly accomplish all dharmas and attain their efficacy—they should attend to and uphold the method for the rosary in this manner."
However, the substances of these beads vary; if one uses iron for the rosary, one obtains five times the merit for each recitation and counting;
if one uses red copper for the rosary, one obtains ten times the merit for each recitation and counting;
if one uses precious materials such as pearls and coral for the rosary, one obtains a hundred times the merit for each recitation and counting.
If one uses *śrīphala* seeds for a rosary, reciting and counting one bead gains a thousandfold merit;
if one uses lotus seeds for a rosary, reciting and counting one bead gains a ten-thousandfold merit;
if one uses *indrakṣa* seeds for a rosary, reciting and counting one bead gains a millionfold merit.
If one uses *ulūkalakṣa* as a rosary, for every single recitation and bead-counting, one obtains a hundred billion times the merit;
if one uses crystal as a rosary, for every single recitation and bead-counting, one obtains a thousand billion times the merit;

if one uses bodhi seeds as a rosary—whether counting them while reciting or merely holding them in the hand—for every single recitation, the merit is immeasurable, incalculable, and beyond comparison.
"If those who wish to be reborn in the pure lands of the various Buddhas desire to do so, they should receive and maintain this bead according to the Dharma.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva said: "Regarding the bodhi-fruit seed (bodhi-jīva):

if there is a person who holds this bodhi-bead in their hand, even if they cannot recite the names of the Buddhas or dharanis according to the Dharma, but merely carry it with them while walking, standing, sitting, or lying down—whatever words they utter, whether good or evil—by virtue of this person holding the bodhi-seed, the merit obtained will be no different from that of reciting the mantras of the Buddhas; they shall obtain immeasurable blessings."
As for this rosary, it must consist of exactly one hundred and eight beads.
If these are difficult to obtain, there may be fifty-four, twenty-seven, or even fourteen; such are the distinctions in the merit of the rosary.
"For what reason do you now specifically praise the use of bodhi seeds as being most excellent for obtaining benefit?
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva replied:
"In the distant past, there was a Buddha who appeared in the world and attained equal and perfect enlightenment beneath this very tree."
At that time, there was a non-Buddhist of wrong views whose mind was corrupted, who slandered the Triple Gem. He had a son who was suddenly struck and killed by a non-human spirit.
The non-Buddhist thought to himself:

"I am currently of wrong views; I do not yet know what spiritual powers the Buddhas possess. Since the Tathāgata has now attained equal and perfect enlightenment beneath this tree, if he is truly a Sage, the tree should manifest a response."
He then took his deceased son and lay him beneath the Bodhi tree, saying these words:
"If the Buddha-tree is holy, my son should revive.
After seven days had passed, as he recited the name of the Buddha, the son revived once more.
The non-Buddhists were filled with joy and praised him, saying:
"The Buddhas possess great supernormal powers such as we have never before seen.
That the Buddha, at the tree of enlightenment, manifests such a rare wonder and such immense majesty is truly inconceivable."

At that time, having heard these matters, the various non-Buddhists abandoned their heterodoxy and returned to the truth; they gave rise to the bodhicitta and believed in the inconceivable spiritual power of the Buddha.
For this reason, the people of the world all called it the "Tree of Prolonging Life.
Thus, the Bodhi tree came to have two names:
first, the Bodhi Tree; second, the Tree of Prolonging Life.
At that time, after the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mañjuśrī had spoken these words, the Buddha said:
"Excellent, excellent, Mañjuśrī!"
"It is as you have said.
At that time, having heard this Sūtra on the Merit of Wearing the Bead, the great assembly was filled with immense joy; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Mañjuśrī Sūtra on the Merit of Counting Beads (Mañjuśrī-mālā-guṇa-parimāṇa-sūtra)
